university_wide.semantics: MIT publishes first-year admissions figures for the institute as a whole. Applicants apply to MIT as a whole, not to a particular major, department, or school.

sources.claim: MIT Facts publishes first-year admissions statistics, including applications and offers of admission.
MIT Admissions explains its admissions statistics and first-year admission context.
MIT Admissions describes admission as institute-wide rather than major-specific.

program_level.notes: MIT does not publish undergraduate major-by-major acceptance data in the official sources listed in the research note.

sources.claim: Applicants apply to MIT as a whole, not to a particular major, department, or school.

university_wide.semantics: Stanford IRDS reports applicant, admit, and matriculant trends for first-time first-year admission. The Common Data Set page publishes applicants, admitted, and enrolled counts for first-year admission.

sources.claim: Stanford IRDS publishes undergraduate admission trends.
Stanford explains that first-year applicants apply to the university as a whole.

program_level.notes: Stanford does not publish undergraduate major-level acceptance data in the official sources listed in the research note. Graduate program dashboards exist, but they are outside the undergrad scope of this group.

sources.claim: Stanford undergrad admission is university-wide rather than major-specific.

university_wide.semantics: Harvard publishes Applicants, Admitted, Admit Rate, and Yield Rate in its Fact Book and admissions statistics pages. Students declare concentrations only after admission, so there is no undergraduate admission-by-major selectivity to publish.

sources.claim: Harvard OIRA Fact Book includes applicants, admitted, admit rate, and yield rate.
Harvard explains that concentrations are declared after admission.

program_level.notes: Harvard does not publish undergraduate concentration-level acceptance data in the official sources listed in the research note because concentrations are declared after admission.

sources.claim: Concentrations are declared after admission, not used as an undergraduate admissions selectivity unit.

university_wide.semantics: Imperial's transparency workbook covers the last five completed UCAS cycles and includes admissions rates, applicants, offers made, places confirmed, BMAT scores, and admissions rate by nationality. The university-wide figure is derived from official undergraduate applications received and new admissions totals.

sources.claim: Imperial transparency and statistics pages list undergraduate admissions data.
Imperial's statistics guide includes undergraduate applications, admissions, and ratio tables.

program_level.notes: Imperial's course-level tables use applications received, new admissions, and applications:admissions ratio, with separate breakdowns by home/overseas and additional dimensions such as nationality and entry qualifications.

sources.claim: Imperial course-level tables include applications received, new admissions, and applications:admissions ratio.
